newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraqi paper attacks U.S., hails Russia.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi paper attacks U.S., hails Russia.

text.p: The ruling Baath party newspaper al-Thawra on Thursday criticised the United States for its tough policy on Iraq and hailed Russia's attitude.

Iraq is under U.N. trade sanctions imposed for its 1991 invasion of Kuwait. Al-Thawra said Washington was adding its own interpretation to a U.N. resolution under which curbs on Iraqi oil exports cannot be lifted until Baghdad eliminates its weapons of mass destruction.
The United States, it said, adopted "double standards" in its Iraq policy linking the lifting of sanctions to political changes in the country.
But Al-Thawra said Russia showed "positive and objective" views linking an end to sanctions on Iraq to its honouring of 1991 Gulf War disarmament terms.

"The Americans have no right at all to come now and add new explanations to (U.N.) Security Council resolutions...and also they have no right to imposes themselves as both legislators and judges at international institutions," it added.
"Russia's stand is objective and represents the international legitimacy," Thawra said.
Russia last month signed a mult-billion dollar oil deal with Iraq and has said it would like to have the oil embargo removed so Baghdad can repay its debts to Moscow.
Iraq currently exports limited amounts of oil for humanitarian purchases under a U.N. deal that went into effect in December.
